newsitem.title: GERMANY: Uninspired Bunds glued into range before holiday.
newsitem.headline: Uninspired Bunds glued into range before holiday.

text.p: Bunds religiously followed U.S. Treasuries lower in late European trade, lacking enthusiasm to break out of their recent range before a national holiday in Germany on Thursday.

With the June DTB future unwilling to venture beyond a narrow scope, analysts said the most players could hope for now would be to see the contract consolidate enough for a push higher early next week.
German markets are closed for the Ascension Day holiday on Thursday and many investors are expected to take advantage of the long weekend and stay away on Friday as well.
Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London, said that with no domestic impetus, Bunds were likely to remain painfully quiet.

"There is reportedly still some good buying interest in the short dates -- in two- and three-year paper -- and technically the (futures) market still looks quite constructive, but other than that the German market is really not doing anything on its own," he said.
By 1420 GMT, the DTB June future was trading 18 basis basis points lower on the day at 101.70, while the cash 10-year benchmark was quoted at 101.63 for a 5.778 percent bid yield.

But on spreads, German squeezed ahead of the U.S. market, pushing the 10-year yield gap out to 105 basis points after U.S. data showed first quarter productivity was up 2.0 percent -- the biggest gain since the fourth quarter of 1993.
The spread was 102 basis points late on Tuesday.

With the Federal Reserve's Beige Book on business conditions due later on Wednesday, German markets must wait until Friday to catch up with any T-bond reaction, which analysts said may mean early Friday trade may be quite lively.
Bunds will hold up relatively well if T-bonds are hit by the report, with German fundamentals supporting, analysts said.
